verdict_reason: The base-2 core implements Atienza et al. Def. 3.1 and agrees with the author-linked GUDHI implementation after unit conversion and with giotto-tda 0.6.2 to maximum absolute error 8.882e-16 on a representative finite-positive parity sweep; it also returns the closed-form 2.000000000000 bits for four equal bars. YELLOW, not GREEN, because the valid finite barcodes [1, 1e-16] and [1e308, 1e308] return 0.0 instead of 5.315084951820e-15 and exactly 1.0 bits, respectively, leaving two concrete value-changing numerical exceptions to the paper formula.
comparable_reason: At the merged 1,000-example default, all 7 locally cached models had exactly 999 finite H0 bars and layer-0 H0 normalized PE only 0.999096280 to 0.999659659 (0.05637% mean-relative span); dividing by the common log2(999) denominator leaves raw and normalized H0 ranks identical. H1 is not comparable as reported: its bar count varied from 730 to 1,119, raw PE varied from 9.061026 to 9.688104 bits, PE versus bar count had Spearman rho=0.936975 (p=0.001851), and raw PE had rho=-0.823329 with width, -0.917779 with depth, and -0.857143 with log parameter count. The normalized H1 variant attenuated those to -0.692345, -0.642445, and -0.821429 but the log-parameter association remained significant (p=0.02345); directly repeating the unchanged [1, 2] lifespan distribution 1 to 100 times moved normalized PE from 0.918296 to 0.989311, so the strict direct-mechanism plus association-reduction gate fails.
normalized_variant: layer_{l}_pe_h0_norm / layer_{l}_pe_h1_norm (PE / log2(number of raw bars))
github_reason: I located the official GUDHI source and executed GUDHI 3.12.0 Entropy, whose documentation points to Atienza et al. and credits coauthor Manuel Soriano-Trigueros's prior implementation. On 203 shared finite-positive diagrams, BLME bits multiplied by ln(2) versus GUDHI had maximum absolute/relative errors 8.882e-16/6.046e-16 nats; I independently fetched and ran giotto-tda 0.6.2 (wheel SHA256 63066e3ab703b0ba6a49e670c2695b087b079674fbe805e584ec6967a8ff1c71), which agreed within 8.882e-16 bits. The edge [1, 1e-16] remained a real BLME mismatch (0.0 versus GUDHI 3.684136148790e-15 nats and giotto-tda 5.315084951820e-15 bits), while [1e308, 1e308] also breaks both references, so executed parity is broad but not a substitute for the analytic domain check.
paper_reason: Chintakunta et al. publish E(F2)=1.474560793 and E(F3)=1.459622430 in natural-log units. Reconstructing their stated filtrations gave BLME 2.127341542919 and 2.105790045882 bits, or 1.474560792562 and 1.459622433154 after multiplication by ln(2), for relative errors 2.969e-10 and 2.161e-09, respectively.
confounds_reason: Across the 7-model current-default sweep, layer-0 H0 was not significantly associated with width (rho=0.355529, p=0.43385), depth (rho=0.128489, p=0.78367), or log parameters (rho=0.500000, p=0.25317), but the co-reported H1 PE was associated with all three: rho=-0.823329 (p=0.02285), -0.917779 (p=0.003560), and -0.857143 (p=0.01370), and with H1 bar count at rho=0.936975 (p=0.001851). Isometric zero-padding of the same 80-point cloud from 8 to 64 and 512 coordinates changed both raw and normalized H0/H1 PE by exactly 0.0, so the formula has no direct ambient-coordinate-count dependence; the confirmed proxy behavior is population-level architecture/bar-count association. Vocabulary was not identifiable because the sweep had only 2 values, 50,257 and 50,304; its apparent H0 rho=0.866025 (p=0.01172) is inseparable from GPT-2 versus Pythia family.
